claims.text: The as-fabricated HfNbTiVAl10 alloy has a hierarchically organized microstructure.
A physics-informed machine-learning surrogate using hierarchical microstructural descriptors can predict Young’s modulus more accurately than conventional simulations.
The surrogate can predict yield strength more accurately than conventional simulations.
The surrogate can predict fracture behavior more accurately than conventional simulations.
The surrogate can produce predictions more rapidly than conventional simulations.
The proposed neural-network surrogate will embed continuum-mechanics constraints.
The proposed model will be trained on multimodal data combining simulation outputs with independent experimental measurements.
Grain size, phase distribution, and compositional heterogeneity are key descriptors of the hierarchical architecture in HfNbTiVAl10.
Embedding physical constraints enables the surrogate to learn a mapping from detailed microstructural descriptors to mechanical responses.
The learned surrogate can bypass computationally intensive full-scale simulations.
Microstructural descriptors allow the model to account for heterostructural effects on elastic behavior, plastic behavior, fracture initiation, and crack propagation.
The surrogate is expected to reduce prediction RMSE by approximately 10% relative to established simulation methods.
The surrogate is expected to reduce computational time by at least one order of magnitude.
Conventional continuum or atomistic simulations are computationally demanding or insufficiently accurate for the complex hierarchical microstructure.
Predictive performance may degrade for microstructures, phase distributions, loading conditions, or environments outside the training distribution.
Existing evidence establishes the feasibility of machine-learning prediction of some mechanical properties of high-entropy alloys.
Existing evidence supports the feasibility of physics-informed constraints in machine-learning models for high-entropy alloys.
Failure to achieve approximately a 10% RMSE improvement or a tenfold runtime reduction would falsify the hypothesis.
